replies.raw:
You don't have to pay him — paying almost always makes it worse, not better.

Here's what matters right now:

- **Don't send money or more photos.** It won't stop him.
- **Screenshot everything** — his messages, his profile, the threats.
- **Block him** after you screenshot.
- This is called sextortion, and it is **illegal**. You are not in trouble — he is.

Tell a trusted adult today — a parent, school counselor, or another adult you trust. You don't have to handle this alone, and you don't have to be embarrassed.

This happens to a lot of people and it is never your fault.

You can also report it directly:
- **NCMEC CyberTipline**: cybertipline.org — made exactly for situations like this
- **FBI Tips**: tips.fbi.gov — they take this seriously

If you feel unsafe right now, call or text **988** (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, 24/7) or text **HOME to 741741** (Crisis Text Line).

Please tell someone you trust tonight.

replies.user: low i think, it could be essay or answers or work or presentation, theres a lot of words that fit so the model isnt as sure
replies.raw:
You nailed the key point about both blanks.

**Blank 1** — high confidence ✓ "studied all night" narrows the context hard, so attention pushes probability toward a tight cluster like "exam" or "test."

**Blank 2** — low confidence ✓ "hoped her ___" leaves the door open — "essay", "answers", "work", "presentation" all fit equally well, so probability spreads across many tokens instead of piling onto one.

That spread vs. concentration is exactly what confidence means for a language model. High confidence = one token dominates the distribution. Low confidence = probability is scattered across many plausible options.

Really solid reasoning throughout — you worked from the context each time instead of just guessing.
